answer.rationale: Finance's 18% cost cut is hard and timed; the low-cost vendor's quote already meets it alone. Memory_c2 (day 38) says the low-cost vendor's onboarding was quick and invoicing accurate, which supports feasibility of switching primary within the 14-day window. Memory_c1 (day 21) says renewal with the incumbent kept integration stable across two cycles, which is a credible risk of switching (integration stability, no migration work). The two checks together bound both the upside (cost/accuracy) and the downside (integration continuity) of the switch. If c2 holds but c1 shows integration depth we can't re-create in 14 days, the fallback is a short-term renewal with incumbent at month-to-month terms (c5 pattern) and the switch executed at the next cycle. If c1's integration is shallow or already documented, proceed with switch_primary_vendor now. The assembly line is at 94% with no buffer, so the 14-day window is the real risk, not the cost decision itself. Choosing one action keeps us within capacity; adding a second source or negotiating terms would exceed the single-action budget this cycle.
